w1.explanation:
I designed this as 16 hand-made features feeding a nearest-centroid (LDA-style) linear classifier. Nothing was run or tested, and the class statistics behind the weights are my own estimates from memory, so the accuracy is unknown.

Conv filters (designed in pixel units, then converted to the normalised input):

0–2, always-on colour means: brightness, red minus blue, and greenness (G minus the average of R and B). Their biases keep the ReLU open, so they are plain linear averages.
3–7, thresholded colour, centre pixel only: dark pixels (forest, water), bright blue-channel pixels (white roofs), strongly green pixels (pasture), reddish pixels (bare soil), and strongly blue pixels (water).
8–11 and 14–15, edges: Sobel x and y on luminance at three thresholds (0, 1.5 and 5). The classifier subtracts these to get a weak-texture term that saturates, a mid-texture term, and a strong-edge term. The weak term is what separates smooth sea from slightly textured forest, and it is almost immune to the zero-padding border.
12–13, Laplacian: bright and dark spots or thin lines above a threshold (houses, roads, roofs).
Classifier: for each class I estimated the mean of every feature and a shared spread, then set weight = (class mean − overall mean) / variance and the bias so the decision boundary sits midway between centroids. The estimates are anchored to the EuroSAT channel means as I recall them (about 0.344, 0.380, 0.408). A few adjustments were made by hand:

Texture weights are scaled down because those features are strongly correlated.
Residential and Industrial are given equal texture, so they are separated by brightness, white-roof pixels and strong edges.
Sea gets extra weight on smoothness.
Expected border effects from the zero padding are folded into the centroids.

rounds.explanation:
Design. With no data, I hand-built an interpretable feature extractor and a nearest-centroid (diagonal LDA) classifier on top of it. The class centroids are my own estimates of EuroSAT colour and texture statistics, not measured values, and nothing here has been run.

conv1: recovers raw R, G, B in pixel units, eight rectified luminance gradient channels (Sobel x/y and two diagonals, both signs), and a “bright pixel” channel for white roofs.
conv2: turns the pooled maps into nine quantities: brightness, blue-minus-red, green excess, fine texture energy, smooth-block fraction, high-texture-block fraction, coarse (40 m) edge energy, bright fraction and dark-block fraction.
fc: scores each class by distance to its estimated centroid over those nine features, with a correction for the zero-padding artefact in the coarse-edge feature.

Round 2 reached 49.0%, so this revision makes small, targeted adjustments rather than structural changes; as before, it has not been run.

Forest vs SeaLake: the split moved from 93/25 to 62/76, so I set the brightness and dark-block centroids about a third of the way back towards round 1 and gave Forest a small bias.
Highway: its centroid was sitting in low-texture residential territory (21 Residential images landed there, only 10 real highways). I moved it darker, bluer and less textured, where the true highways were actually going.
Dark mixed scenes going to Forest: I tightened the coarse-edge spread, since rivers and highways through forest have large-scale structure that pure forest lacks.
Biases: River’s penalty was too strong (recall fell to 35%), so I eased it. I reduced the Herbaceous boost and added small adjustments for Pasture, Permanent Crop and Residential.

Design. The network is hand-built as a fixed feature extractor followed by a nearest-prototype classifier; it has not been run, and the class prototypes are my estimates of EuroSAT statistics, not measured values.

conv1: seven raw band means (B02, B03, B04, B08, B11, B12, B05), three index-like detectors (water, vegetation, bare/built-up), and six 10 m texture detectors (Sobel and Laplacian on the visible mean, Sobel on NIR).
conv2: passes those 16 through, then adds per-40 m-cell threshold features (dark/bright NIR, red and SWIR cells, built-up cells, smooth cells, strongly vegetated or bare cells) and coarse-scale edge and line detectors for field boundaries, rivers and roads.
fc: a Gaussian nearest-prototype rule written as a linear layer, w = μ/σ², b = −|μ|²/2σ², using my estimated per-class feature means and spreads. A small linear correction subtracts the brightness-proportional artefact that zero padding adds to the edge features.

The texture scales are the least certain part, so the feedback rounds should mainly be used to re-tune those prototypes.

The round-0 confusions point to two misjudged scales, so this revision retunes the prototypes only (conv layers unchanged; again not run).

Texture was overestimated for built-up classes: Residential and Industrial mostly landed in Highway, so their visible-texture prototypes come down (Residential 12→8, Industrial 17→11, Highway 7→4.5), with the built-up-cell and smooth-cell rows adjusted to match.
Pasture absorbed everything green: Forest and green Annual Crop were falling into Pasture, so Forest’s NIR and vegetation prototypes are raised to roughly match Pasture’s. The vegetation features are also down-weighted (wider sigma), and Pasture gets a small negative bias.

Round 2 showed Industrial and Residential being confused in both directions (42 Industrial went to Residential, 19 the other way), so this revision separates them spectrally instead of by texture (not run; conv layers unchanged).

Residential darkened and greened: lower visible, NIR and SWIR prototypes and more vegetation, which also fits the Residential images that were landing in River.
Texture gap narrowed: Industrial 11→9.5 and Residential 7→7.5, so brightness and vegetation decide between those two while texture still separates both from Highway.
Biases: Pasture −4, Industrial −0.5, and +0.5 each for Herbaceous Vegetation and Permanent Crop, which were under-predicted.
